Task.Prompt: Draw and label a square with a prescribed nonzero side AB and a square inscribed in a circle. Record steps, diagonals and proofs for both. Start by writing a conjecture about square diagonals.

Criteria.Criterion: Valid nonzero base AB and two perpendiculars on same side
Transfers exact radius AB to both auxiliary rays and joins square in order
Inscribed circle construction with two perpendicular diameters and labelled vertices
Justifies equal sides, right angles, perpendicular equal bisected diagonals

Task.Accept: Two correct labelled square constructions with equal-side/right-angle proofs
Task.Reject: visual rectangle without equal sides, arbitrary diamond, missing bisected/perpendicular diameters

FirstPartyCooldown.Prompt: Edulytiks-authored Cool-down (publisher teacher original not read): given a circle of radius 3, construct two perpendicular diameters and connect their four endpoints in cyclic order to make a square. Explain why the diagonals meet at right angles, are congruent and bisect one another, and why the square's sides are congruent; teacher scores actual labelled construction.

Transfers exact radius AB to both auxiliary rays and joins square in order

Items.Prompt: All squares are regular polygons, but not all rectangles or rhombi are; give counterexamples.
Items.Expected: Regular needs equal sides AND angles; square yes, nonsquare rectangle unequal sides and oblique rhombus unequal angles.

Items.Prompt: Why use a circle centred A through B when constructing a square with AB as a side?
Items.Expected: The circle transfers length AB onto the perpendicular through A to mark another side exactly equal.

Items.Prompt: After constructing a perpendicular through off-line C to AB, what creates the parallel through C?
Items.Expected: Construct the line through C perpendicular to the first perpendicular.

Items.Prompt: A learner's circle is tangent to the base line and has only one intersection. Why does the bisector procedure fail?
Items.Expected: An auxiliary chord needs two distinct intersections; increase radius beyond point-to-line distance.

Items.Prompt: Why must equal-distance marks on two sides of an angle share the same vertex B?
Items.Expected: The construction uses points P,Q with BP=BQ so the interior equal-radius intersection makes triangles BPX and BQX congruent.

Items.Prompt: How do two intersecting equal-radius circles centred A,B produce an equilateral triangle?
How can a straightedge and compass bisect positive segment AB?
Items.Expected: Choose arcs of common radius r>AB/2 from A,B, connect two intersections; their line crosses AB at midpoint.

TeacherAcknowledgement: Teacher receives the physical paper and verifies construction and reasoning; assigns rubric 0/1/2 for each criterion, signs/dates feedback. Student submission/grade does not run online by this contract.

Cases.CORRECT: equal side lengths and four 90° angles, circle-inscribed vertices and valid diagonal relations
Cases.EQUIVALENT: clockwise/anticlockwise, reflection, rotation, other positive side lengths
Cases.WRONG: rhombus counted as square without angle proof, circles tangent where two intersections needed
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: numbers or diagram without construction steps and proof

StageD.Missing: secure school/pathway lesson-assigned paper review and persisted teacher score, authenticated visual/tenant E2E
